why: The RL change acts only through signed weights times the input directions the text excites, so a constant per-layer vector with no input dependence closes little of KL(RL||base) on cued-base text.
Same input-gated mechanism on RL text: a constant per-layer shift cannot reproduce a text-dependent change, so it closes only a small share.
A constant vector on the MLP output alone carries even less of the input-gated MLP change, so it closes a small share on cued-base text.
Same as t59 on RL text: an input-independent MLP offset closes a small share of KL.

Code-RL's task lives in its signs, which agree with Math-RL's only at chance on the shared entries, and its effect is gated by code-rollout input directions, so on math text it stays near the plain base's 224.
For the same reason Code-RL adds no math gain on top of the cue, leaving the cued Code-RL model near the cued base's 410.
A random difference of matched norm has random signs on a random mask, so it carries no task signal and leaves the cued base at its 410.
With no task signal in a random-sign difference, the cued base's length behaviour is unchanged from its 3,933 tokens per problem.
The RL change is gated by the kind of text (math solution), not by correctness, so peaks of the base-RL difference rarely sit at the first wrong step.
